quest.title: Where Our Space and Time Intersect
quest.description: In this unfamiliar world, with companions beyond reach... What path is there to take that leads back to their side?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1425, Mora x62225, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act VII
chapter.title: A Traveler on a Winter's Night

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What just happened...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Nasha Town? How did I get here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Strange. I remember being trapped by Dottore during the battle... And now, all of a sudden, I'm here.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Something weird is going on... I guess I'll start by exploring the area.)

dialogues.speaker: Katya
dialogues.text: #Hmm? {NICKNAME}? What brings you here at this hour?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Katya
dialogues.text: What are you in the mood for today? A hot dog? Or something else? We've got some special discounts at the moment — you wanna see the menu?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry, I'm not hungry right now.

dialogues.speaker: Katya
dialogues.text: Ah. Well, feel free to take a seat for now. Let me know if you change your mind.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Everyone seems to be acting normal... Am I just overthinking?)

dialogues.speaker: Borzyslaw
dialogues.text: #Oh! Darling, look who it is! One of our regular customers. Get {NICKNAME} something to eat, would you, dear?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Wait... Why is he talking like that...?)

dialogues.speaker: Katya
dialogues.text: I'd love to, but can't serve a customer unless they order something. Anyway, I take it your business is wrapped up?

dialogues.speaker: Borzyslaw
dialogues.text: Yes thankfully. It was a long trip, and it's left me feeling pretty exhausted. But the upshot is, I won't have to leave again for a good while. We can have some quality time to ourselves!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Wait... these two are a couple? I see some kids around, too. I didn't know they had a family...)

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: Hey there! I haven't seen you in ages... What's keeping you so busy? I've been looking forward to playing with you again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Have we met?

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: You forgot already? Heh, you're silly! Daddy brought you over to our house recently. We had some snacks together.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...What is she talking about?)

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: We've had a lot of customers over the last few days, so we've been real busy. And like my Mom always says — some people are more than just customers. They're friends.

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: Oh! Another customer's arrived. I'd better go see what they want!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This is all wrong. I never once heard the owner of this restaurant talk about their family. It certainly isn't a family-run business... And that child? I don't recognize her at all...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Could this be... a false memory?)
Very good. I knew you had it in you.

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: Aren't you going to try the house special?

response.speaker: The Doctor
response.text: You don't seem to like it here. That's fine... we can change venues.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...I'm still alive...?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Where is this place? It took all my strength to open the Moon Gate, and then I leapt into it...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (So this is... the moon's reflection? The mysterious realm beyond the gate?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (...Hmm. I can't sense anything.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (I guess I could try opening the gate once more?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...! *panting*

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (No response... Maybe this space can't be opened from inside.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Hmm... If this was the space that killed both Rerir and his lover... Then why am I unscathed?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Or... No, I'm not unscathed. Even the air here feels... frozen in place. There is nothing here with which I can restore my power...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (...I should conserve my strength and proceed with caution.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (I don't believe Dottore's scheming will stop just because I escaped. If there is any chance that I can get back to the others, any chance at all...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...I must return.

talks.objective: Use your power to interact with the mysterious phenomenon
Enter the world in the mirror
Explore the world in the mirror
Explore the world in the mirror

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Goodbye for now, Columbina. I hope you have a wonderful night.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I will.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Lauma, everyone else... and me?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Are these... my memories?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (I can't touch them... It's as if we're separated by some impenetrable power...)

dialogues.speaker: Kaarina
dialogues.text: Haha! Over here, over here!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (But the people in these memories pass right through me. Just like when I disappeared...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (If only I had known what would come to pass after that...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (...Even so, I should still take a look around. Just being back here... It gives me the strength to keep going.)

talks.objective: Explore the world in the mirror
Explore the world in the mirror

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Please, draw the first Lunar Arcana. This represents "destiny," and is the foundation for the divination as a whole.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (My "destiny"... I believe the card I drew was "The Moon.")

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Now that I think about it, Barbeloth's divination was absolutely right...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Ah, it's almost time to draw the last card. The one that represents the "future"...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (That was the card that popped out on its own. From here, I think...)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Hmm? A... kuuvahki pulse?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Fascinating. I've never encountered this before in my role as a diviner...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (What's going on? Did that card leave the deck... because of my influence?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (All I did was try to touch it, and then...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Maybe this memory space is not untouchable after all... are there weak points in the barrier?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Or... is it possible that there's more to this space than my memories alone?)

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: ...This card is "Death."

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (...I need to get to the bottom of this.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (I'll try touching something else... Hmm?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Is this... the wind? No! It's gravity! It's pulling me outwards...!)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #No! ...{NICKNAME}!

talks.objective: Explore the world in the mirror
Analyze the current situation with your companions
Analyze the current situation with your companions

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...Paimon, listen to me.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: #From the bottom of our hearts, we're so, so sorry... We completely understand how you must feel. {NICKNAME} is trapped, and we all feel responsible for it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Don't say that... Paimon's not a little kid. You didn't leave {M#him}{F#her} behind on purpose — there was nothing you could do...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... But... *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{M#He}{F#She}'s all alone in there. What if something happens to {M#him}{F#her}? What are we gonna do then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #We've barely spent any time apart since we met... Is {M#he}{F#she}... Is {M#he}{F#she} gonna... die?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: #We must find a way to rescue {M#him}{F#her}. We were all involved in the operation where {M#he}{F#she} was captured, and we do not abandon our comrades.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: That being said, it won't be easy. Through conversation with the others on our return, we've arrived at a basic idea of what we're up against.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Dottore's lab has clearly been in operation for a lot longer than we realized. We found many monster samples stored there — in all likelihood, they were materials he used to research his latest technology.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: We also know that through his contact with the phantoms of Hyperborea, he gained knowledge about the moons and certain Hyperborean technologies.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Using this knowledge, he then fashioned an artificial Moon Marrow to serve as a replacement for the Frost Moon beyond the sky.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Unlike Columbina, Dottore is not being rejected by Teyvat. And even with two of the three Moon Marrows, his power far exceeds all of ours combined.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Once his third Moon Marrow is complete, Dottore will have completely seized the authority of the three moons. Teyvat's most primordial powers will then be in his grasp.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: D—Does that mean...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: I'm afraid so. ...No one could have predicted this level of insanity, not even from Dottore. And unfortunately, his insanity is coupled with an intellect and ambition that not even his peers in the Fatui can match.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...This is dire. Sounds like the world is done for.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The three moons' authority can influence the very fabric of time and space... I dare not imagine what a monster like him would do with that kind of power.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The trouble's already begun, I'm afraid. On our way back, we discovered that part of Nod-Krai is being enveloped by an unknown energy. We cannot ascertain what is happening inside.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm convinced this is Dottore's doing, not that there's any way to prove it. The issue is, we have no idea what his intentions are.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: The only thing more frustrating than facing down evil is knowing that it will surely come, but not knowing when.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: The Doctor is guilty of numerous crimes in Mondstadt as well. One of our knights— well, former knights... His father was murdered by Dottore.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: His ideology and methodology are a danger to everything in his path, from individuals to entire nations. He does not feel guilt, even when he acts against his own people.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: He doesn't see them as his own people, that's why. People like him see everyone else as beneath them.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Right. He views other people only in terms of how they can benefit him. That's the basis of all his social connections.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Granted, he's hardly the only harbinger to pursue their own interests. We all do — and Her Majesty is gracious enough to permit it. Still, her mercy has its limits.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Dottore's actions have gone beyond even what the Fatui could have imagined. Usurping divine authority to become a god? For a servant of the Tsaritsa, that goes beyond being disloyal. It's treason of the highest order.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: We can't expect him to heed the Tsaritsa's will once he gains the three moons' authority. Even we harbingers consider him the most self-interested among us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Poor {NICKNAME}... of all the people to get caught by... We have to go save {M#him}{F#her}, right now! Please, we gotta find a way!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Paimon, I promise you, we are with you all the way.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I get how you feel. I do. But it's gonna take more than strong emotions to take down an enemy like Dottore. What we need now is more information.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: #Right. We can't even guarantee he's still at his research center. Before we can think about mounting a rescue operation, we need to confirm {NICKNAME}'s location.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...I'll find a way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon knows... But, but... She's so scared... If anything happens to {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{M#He}{F#She} might be the strongest person Paimon knows, but {M#he}{F#she}'s still human. {M#He}{F#She} feels pain and bleeds just like anyone else...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Then think things through before you stick your neck out! Unless you wanna lose your head!

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Miss Sandrone. You're okay?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Put the stuff over there. And be gentle with it.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Am I okay! Huh! As you can see, I've had to move my whole livelihood out of the Experimental Design Bureau. It's been swallowed up by Dottore's energy field. If I'd left it any longer, I probably would've gotten stuck there.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Ugh. Dottore always goes a little loco when he finds a shiny new toy — not that he'd ever admit that. But this time, he's gone full psycho.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sob*... *sniff*...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Just go ahead and cry already.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry... Paimon's not trying to make a scene, it's just, it's just... she can't... *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Let it all out. There's no shame in it. When you're overwhelmed by fear and despair, crying can help get it out of your system. You'll feel better for it.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Okay then. While the baby of the group is having a moment, how about the grown-ups get to work? Give me your hand.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: You've made a discovery?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Pulonia, scan.

dialogues.speaker: Pulonia
dialogues.text: (Scans)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You, hand. Now.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Oh, I thought you'd never ask, my lady.

dialogues.speaker: Pulonia
dialogues.text: (Scans)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Curses!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You're next, then you.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As Sandrone scans everyone who took part in the battle against Dottore, her face contorts with displeasure.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Dottore, you son of a... He's done something to us! Everyone who entered his research center has been implanted with some sort of curse.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I don't feel anything unusual at the moment. Does that mean it hasn't activated yet? Is there a way to figure out its purpose and what might trigger it?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: My best guess is Dottore created it using the moon goddess's powers. One second, analyzing...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Ugh! That frigging maniac!

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: So. What twisted game is he playing this time?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: The moment I analyzed the energy composition, some encrypted text appeared in my mind's eye...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: And when I deciphered it according to the Fatui's standard encryption protocol, I got the following message... "Feel free to run. Or, you will perish in Nod-Krai."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: He's mocking us.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yup. He loves to toy with people. Only in this case, there might be more to it.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But I didn't detect any murderous intent or malice either in the message or the curse's energy... As if, this is him at his least malicious.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Or perhaps all people are cowards in his eyes. Maybe he thinks the threat alone will be effective.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: #What a despicable person... and he has {NICKNAME} in his grasp.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: If I may... As unhinged as Dottore may be, he has always exercised great patience with the objects of his interest.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: #I remember a comment he made when we first arrived in Nod-Krai... He said, this world is, on the whole, an exceedingly dull place. But at least there are a few intriguing features — such as the gods, or {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Presumably, they interest him because they're unknown quantities. He wants to understand as much as he can about them.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: #Agreed. {NICKNAME} is Teyvat's Fourth Descender — all harbingers are aware of this.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: #Since Dottore took such pains to capture {NICKNAME}, he is unlikely to kill {M#him}{F#her} right away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Okay, but we still have to do that rescue operation!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Of course. I also think we need to read between the lines with Dottore's message. If he's encouraging us to run, that means we mustn't leave Nod-Krai under any circumstances.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: My guess is, his curse will only trigger if we leave.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: We've discovered multiple energy fields. Albedo is still attempting to analyze their structure. He told me to report back first.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Each field is slowly growing, swallowing up more of the surrounding area in the process. And the pace of their expansion has increased since we first examined them... He's probably trying to swallow Nod-Krai whole.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: His nefarious ambition knows no bounds... If this continues, the whole of Teyvat will be in trouble, not just Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The loss of Columbina could not have come at a worse time... Do we... do we think she's truly gone for good?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: She entered the space beyond the Moon Gate, knowing what became of Rerir and Tholindis... I'm sorry, but... I fear the odds aren't good.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Don't be ridiculous! If I know her, she's busy finding a way back as we speak just so she can annoy me. Hah, she isn't dead!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Whatever has become of her, the fact remains that we are two comrades short on the eve of a decisive battle.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: #We need to find out {NICKNAME}'s location. But there is also other work to be done.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Agreed. Whatever Dottore's planning, we have to get the local populace somewhere safe. So as well as a rescue mission, we have to organize a mass evacuation at the same time.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: It would be best if someone could approach leaders of neighboring nations and negotiate emergency asylum for Nod-Krai's inhabitants. Can anyone handle that?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Snezhnaya is one option. I'll see what I can do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #This'd be so much easier if {NICKNAME} was here... No, stop thinking like that, Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon will join you! She's pretty well-connected thanks to {NICKNAME}. Maybe it'll come in handy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Either way, that's what {NICKNAME} would do if {M#he}{F#she} was here.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Back here again...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (That gravitational force that pulled me back... Is this where it came from?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (When I saw that "memory" of Moon-Prayer Night... I think I influenced reality. Was it just a coincidence? Or...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (If only I could've sent the others some kind of warning on Moon-Prayer Night... Maybe we could have stopped Dottore...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (I feel... so heavy... Does entering that space consume a lot of energy?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Well, even so... I have to keep moving forward.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Back to emptiness and silence again... I should try and find my way back inside that memory...)

talks.objective: Enter the world in the mirror
Explore the world in the mirror
Explore the world in the mirror

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what do we do next?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Wait! That voice... Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The most important thing right now is to find that mage...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #Lauma, {NICKNAME}, and Mr. Varka are here too!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I'd better go pay the Fatui a visit...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}!

talks.objective: Explore the world in the mirror

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Suddenly, I've been plunged into darkness, alone.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It feels strange... As if something has grabbed hold of me. Is Dottore now powerful enough to interfere with space itself?)

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Look at you, standing so still in total silence. I almost didn't recognize you.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: #Hello there, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (He seems to be in a good mood... Wait, what's that behind him?)

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Ah, so you noticed. This is the completed Trilune — two primordial Moon Marrows and one artificial specimen.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: You're wary of it. Good. Maintain that reverence.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: You performed well in that recent battle. Brave and reckless, as always.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Courage is the sign of a true hero, and impulsiveness is the hallmark of those who strive to advance. I say this not to belittle you — most creatures are far more timid by comparison.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Three Moon Marrows? Does that mean... the artificial one is now complete too?)

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Well spotted. What do you think? For a replica I built myself, I daresay it looks the part.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Dottore. Are you planting illusions in my mind?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I have no interest in fooling your eyes. On the contrary, I hope to show you the true essence of all that you see before you.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Is this not a beautiful city? People live in peace and find joy in their work. The streets are safe — people can even leave their doors unlocked at night. You might say it is the Elysium everyone dreams of.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: All available data indicates that your values and worldview conform with the mainstream. This kind of society should be quite to your taste.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: False beauty is deceitful. Lies are to no one's taste.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Hmm. I wonder, is it your moral standards that are too high? Or your expectations of reality?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Answer me this: If someone existed in a sweet dream from the moment they were born, a dream in which they never once felt pain, which do you think they would consider superior? The dream, or reality?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's pure sophistry. It has nothing to do with your actions!

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Mmm. As I suspected. You have yet to understand all of this for what it really is.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you want from me?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: You sound impatient... Do you think the only reason I'm keeping you is because I want something from you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If it's not, then why haven't you killed me yet? No one can stop you if you're as powerful as a god.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I'm delighted that you recognize that fact.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I believe we last squared off in Sumeru. Ah, the memories... How time flies. You and I have both grown.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I'm not surprised that Arlecchino and Sandrone worked with you. You've always a way of slowly but surely ingratiating yourself with all levels of society.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: People laud you as a hero, but I suspect there's more to it than that. Oh — but to be clear, I don't say that to flatter you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you always give your opponent an appraisal before you deal the final blow?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Call it a long-time habit. I'm a researcher, and one of my duties is to give an objective assessment of my subjects.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: But you misunderstand. We are not opponents — not at this moment.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I just want to talk. Think back to Tartaglia, Arlecchino, Capitano, Columbina, and now, even Sandrone...

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: You've worked with each of them in the past. I believe you can work with me as well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What makes you so sure?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Well, why not? Should the good associate only with the good, and the bad befriend only the bad? I like to think we could have a more mature relationship than that.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Surely you don't think all your relationships are grounded in friendship or shared ideals? People come together because it benefits them to do so. If you think of the people you admire, you must surely admit that they have provided some benefit to you.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Morality, ambition, dreams... People have plenty of words to embellish the nature of their relationships. But once you break free from these ethical frameworks, you will see that the only thing connecting the two of you is mutual benefit.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: And that is what I'd like to talk to you about.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (We're finally getting into it. He's probably been planning to kidnap me for a long time now... but for what, exactly?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (He has the authority of all three moons... I won't be able to gain the upper hand in a fight. Best if I pretend that I'm willing to negotiate for now.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You say you're a god, but you also speak of "mutual benefit." What could a god want that the three moons cannot provide?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Excellent question. But before I answer, I would ask you the same thing.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Gaining Columbina's allegiance was a rare and extraordinary feat. But the Moon Marrows are now in my hands — and I have the edge over her, for this artificial moon is not being rejected by Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Her identity and lineage may have been a thing of glory in the Old World, but they were also shackles that prevented her from ever integrating into Teyvat. I, on the other hand... You may view me as a thief, but I have overcome that limitation.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: So what is it that the three moons cannot grant you? What stops you from negotiating with me to get what you want?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't make deals with lying psychopaths.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: That's quite an accusation. Are you expecting me to get angry with you? Hmm. Well, this is one aspect in which my personal growth has served me well.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: In the past, my less mature self might have been disappointed — perhaps even angry — over a small setback like this. Like when you and Lesser Lord Kusanali joined forces to oppose me, for example.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: But things are different now. Just as the rich do not quibble with the poor, I no longer find myself perturbed by these trivial affairs.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Humans relationships end with conflicts of emotions and interests. But relations between humans and gods are different, and ours is even more unique.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I have ascended to the highest heights and laid claim to unprecedented horizons, and you were no ordinary person to begin with.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Allow me to show you the world, Descender.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Someone of your talent and experience must surely know of the Four Great Rulers who serve the Heavenly Principles. They govern Life, Death, Time, and Space.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: One wounded by a blade will die from blood loss or infection, and one who falls into a lake will drown in agony. The elderly wallow in solitude, and the solitary age faster. Eventually, new life is born, only to embark on the same path of suffering.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: These four divisions anchor the world and shackle those who live in it. But they themselves transcend its boundaries, squandering the power bestowed by the heavens.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: All who live yearn for equality, but unless the gods prostrate themselves and profess that they are mere servants of the living, equality can never exist.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Who makes the rules we must live by? Who has the right to restrict us?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: You know, I heard recently that a group of critics reviewed countless stories and drew an interesting conclusion: They found that it is more often than not the villains who strive tirelessly to push the boundaries of progress.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: In fact, long before this, someone voiced a similar idea in an Akademiya editorial. I felt a great affinity with this perspective. I have never been afraid to step up and play the role of the villain.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Fanatics are trampled down for their transgressions, and those who transcend are rebuked for their audacity. And so, the majority of creatures are too timid to follow my lead.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: But all sacrifices made during my experiments have been worthwhile, as you can now see. I can offer you something new, something unique, precisely because I am a villain.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Think about it. We are eternally bound through mutual interest. Can you truly say you would never turn to malice if it could give you the life you dream of?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: After all, what value do perfection and purity really have? They are fragile and feeble things. Utterly tedious.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I say, better to be governed by a flawed humanity than a Gnosis. The true seeker of knowledge is the villain who undergoes countless tribulations in pursuit of their goal.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I'm sure many people have told you that you're different.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Because I'm a Descender?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Exactly. Very clever.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But what has that got to do with you?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I do not conceal my wicked deeds, my selfish desires, or my greed. A true researcher must act as I do if they are to understand and speak of the truth.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: And yet, a knowledge-seeker like myself will inevitably grow tired of studying Teyvat beyond a point.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: You have traveled to all corners of the world and met many people. Along the way, there have been moments when you were misunderstood, or even became a wanted criminal, and all the while, you have spent your days doing some of the most mundane jobs in the world.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: You fight and toil, claim minuscule rewards from my friend Panta{RUBY#[D]Regrator}lone, then you fight some more, winning some battles and losing others as your search goes on. And this cycle continues with no end in sight...

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Surely, you must sometimes grow weary of being stuck in this same loop day after day?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're completely different. I embrace everything that life throws at me. I am engaged in every step of my journey.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: How does that make us different? I, too, embrace what life brings, researching everything that interests me.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Think of all the novel things I've managed to create — like the artificial Moon Marrow. Don't you see? As unique a specimen as she was, even Columbina is not irreplaceable.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Take that back! She's gone because of your actions!

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I didn't say that to anger you. Though admittedly, I don't see what there is to be angry about. Anything Columbina could do for you, I can do better.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: #I know what your ultimate goal is. You wish to walk the path your {M#sister}{F#brother} walked, and seek answers from {M#her}{F#him} at the end of that journey, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #Someone like you could never understand what it feels like to care about another person the way I care about {M#her}{F#him}.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: #Perhaps not. But that doesn't mean I can't help. I could find your {M#sister}{F#brother} right now, bring {M#her}{F#him} before you, and make {M#her}{F#him} give you the answers you seek.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't be so presumptuous. You'll never begin to understand the situation between us!

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Oh no, this is no presumption. I'm only offering what I know is possible with the power of the Trilune.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: But it seems like you would sooner continue with your journey through this world... Why?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Do you truly desire this journey? Or is it simply a necessary process from which you cannot escape?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Think of all the time and energy you have spent, everything you've had to endure just to make it this far. Is this really what you want? Or has your hand been forced by the promise of that final answer?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Yes, you have made many friends, but do they ever spare a thought for the void in your heart and what it yearns for?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: What you want is not friends — it is family. But do they know this?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I, on the other hand, am far more considerate. Join my experiment, and in return, I will bring your meaningless journey and all its struggles to an end.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...This is a malicious attempt to manipulate me. But at the same time, he's stating some very human truths.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Of course he's right about my predicament. How can I deny it? I have faced ungrateful strangers, never-ending troubles, an endless quest for answers...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #(I want to see {M#her}{F#him}. After everything I've been through, words can't describe how much I miss {M#her}{F#him}, how much I want to be reunited with {M#her}{F#him}.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Wherever you are right now... Do you miss me, too?)

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Alright, everyone. Our next mission is clear: We need to contact all the major organizations, explain the situation to the public, and then begin the evacuation.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: The residents of Nod-Krai are quite dispersed. The two most populated areas are the Southern Isles and Piramida.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Miss Lauma, I will leave Hiisi Island and Nasha Town in your hands. I will liaise with the Fatui and Piramida.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Agreed.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: We will reach out to Natlan and Snezhnaya. Anyone found north of the Experimental Design Bureau should follow the Fatui to Snezhnaya.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: As for those dwelling south of that line, I will ask the Voynich Guild to help persuade them to leave. Then I, Mr. Varka, and the Frostmoon Scions will escort them to Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The Voynich Guild has dealings with the Curatorium of Secrets. I will send them a letter vouching for your credibility.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Jahoda, you should help Lauma. This is too big of a task for one person.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: My wish has come true... You're willingly lending me your most capable employee for the day.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Well, good for you if all this only takes a day. Of course, if it takes any longer, I'll be charging a fee.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Boss, wait! Don't I get a say in this?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Oh, I'm sorry. Something to add, Jahoda?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Well... No one's more important to me than you, Boss. And remember how Lauma healed your eyes after that big battle? I think that's worth at least two or three days' work for the Frostmoon Scions.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...Are you completely incapable of acting in your own self-interest? Or do you simply devalue your own labor?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Are you sure you don't wanna come with us?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Who will see to our other work if we're all busy evacuating residents? Sandrone insists that Columbina is still alive, and we have a Traveler to rescue. There's much to be done.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: But Boss... I'm just worried that...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Well, Nefer, I'll link up with you once my tasks are complete.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What makes you think I'd need you to do that?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I'll need it. And considering the way you approach certain matters, I think you'll be better off with me present.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That's quite enough. Just focus on your work first.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: I bet we're in for an uphill battle here... But we can help out, too! Ineffa and I are gonna help Nasha Town's residents carry their stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Loading schedule: Store essential local research data and technology samples, then, escort the people to Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Understood. I will execute this to the best of my abilities.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Great stuff. Thank you, ladies.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I've contacted the Lightkeepers. A colleague of mine will join us shortly. I will persuade them to conduct a thorough search of the region to ensure that no civilians get left behind.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: As for me... I guess I'll be making an early return to Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I think it's important that someone informs the Dendro Archon of what's going on in Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Roger that. Someone should inform Mondstadt, too. Mr. Durin, can I trust you to handle that? I think you fly faster than any of us can run.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: As an added incentive — get there fast enough, and I'll see about getting your gliding exam waived.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Really? Mission accepted, Sir!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I intend to stay behind and help Miss Sandrone with her research. She has some alchemy-related questions that she'd like me to explore.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: She recognizes your expertise, then. I wish you a fruitful collaboration.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Thank you. In truth, I was surprised to hear her express an interest in subject matter outside of machines.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: I believe she has been investigating some Fontainian technology recently. She made a point of bringing the relevant materials with her when she left the Experimental Design Bureau. She's sorting through everything in her room as we speak.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I should mention that we have one other friend who isn't present. He hasn't made his position in all of this clear, but if we know anything about him, he's likely investigating on his own.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: #Paimon's been very quiet today... But I know how close she and {NICKNAME} are with the Natlanese. She should come with us to the border.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay! Paimon'll do her best!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Make sure to heed Sandrone's warning. Many of us have been cursed by Dottore. As such, under no circumstances should anyone cross national borders. Remain within Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: That aside — personally, I have faith in Columbina... Things look grim, sure, but who knows how it'll play out?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: #Same goes for rescuing {NICKNAME}. Both of them are important allies and friends. We'll be counting on you to gather intel on them, Miss Nefer.
Ah, wonderful. You're all here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That voice again... Nicole?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Whoa, that was loud. And it came out of nowhere... So mysterious.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Sorry, this is the only way I can speak to you all right now. Please accept my apology... Anyway, time is short. I'll cut to the chase.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: We're still facing quite a catastrophe here at the world's borders. Alice has roped in every Hexenzirkel member she can get a hold of — except for me. She told me I had to come and help you all out as a matter of urgency.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I quote: "You love talking, don't you? Well, now it's finally your time to shine! Take these — make sure the whole party gets one each. You'll be in charge of making sure everyone stays connected."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Is this... a Dodocommunication Device?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Scanning... Unknown device... Analyzing... Unknown device... Conclusion: Cute...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Affirmative. It is cute and good. I believe that I quite like it.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: This is no ordinary Dodocommunication Device! It's my very own special modified version! Specifically... Ah, sorry — I almost went off on another tangent there. Anyway, help yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: It will allow us to communicate over long-distances within Nod-Krai. No more worrying about shuttling messages back and forth.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: What astounding technology... Am I right in assuming that it relies on your personal abilities to function, Miss Nicole?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Yes, exactly! Right on cue, Albedo. Ah, I'd love to brag to you all about how it all works... But no. Next time, next time. Anyway, I'll be right with you all, serving as a communication hub.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: That's all from me. Head off as soon as you're ready. I'll be staying here to keep watch... and I'll be sending you my blessings.

talks.objective: Go to the place agreed upon with the Lightkeepers
Go to the place agreed upon with the Lightkeepers

dialogues.text: Ah, Sir Flins. Perfect timing. I just arrived myself.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: You are most considerate, Master Illuga. But in fact, I know you have been sitting here for quite some time.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: ...If you saw me, why didn't you say something?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I was curious to see how long you could sit still for. Also, shouldn't you have managed to sense me approaching?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: That would be a first. You always seem to appear out of thin air without making a peep.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Also, how many times do I have to tell you not to address me as "Master"? I don't qualify.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I beg to differ. Why should a young man so well-versed in social graces as yourself not be worthy of that title?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Please Lord Flins— Uh, Sir Flins! I'm begging you, don't flatter me into complacency like you do with everyone else!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: You understand me better than most. My newest acquaintances tell me I love complimenting others... What do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: I think they don't understand why you do it. You just love puffing people up till they're a big, happy ball of hot air that floats away into the sky.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: In all sincerity, I can only hope that they bring good tidings when they come back down to earth.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Is the situation that bad?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: We just held a strategy meeting. Let me fill you in...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Flins recounts the meeting and the action plan to Illuga.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: ...In short, we need everyone gone from Piramida. We also need a team of Lightkeepers to scour the more remote regions of Nod-Krai for civilians to evacuate.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I only hope we have enough personnel.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: We do. Old Man Nikita will definitely help, and we can recall anyone out on patrol to focus on this instead.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Good. I'm sure you and the others will make short work of this. Now, don't forget — once you've completed this task, make sure you and the rest of the team evacuate to either Snezhnaya or Natlan as well.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Um... Flins?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: If you've got something to say, Master Illuga, why not guess what I'm thinking right now?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: You mentioned that you have... something else to deal with later.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: How... how difficult is it going to be?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I doubt it will be easy.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: I know you're a Lightkeeper, and it's your duty to protect others in times of crisis. But I have a feeling that you'll be walking into grave danger...

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: However bad things have gotten in the past, Nod-Krai has never faced a mass evacuation before. But from the sounds of it, you don't intend to come with us.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: ...I don't mean to pry, and it's probably none of my business. But whatever it is you're intending... you don't have to go through with it, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I've been afflicted with some sort of curse, and I'm told it may well trigger if I set foot outside of Nod-Krai. As such, I cannot leave. I have to act, if for no other reason than to fight this curse.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: What!? N—No... Why? Why would anyone want to curse you?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: There are plenty of people out there willing to trample over others in pursuit of their own goals.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Frankly, Sir Flins, I am furious. You're making light of what is an incredibly serious situation.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Indeed, I am. And?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: And what? I told you, I'm furious about this!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hm. Nothing I can do about it, I'm afraid. Things happen, and we just have to deal with them. If you find yourself feeling angry, perhaps start by drinking a big glass of water?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Hey! You mean you're completely unmoved by my anger? I'm devastated!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Then allow me to express my sincerest regret. Come by the lighthouse sometime. We'll catch ourselves a few fish, have a little barbecue, play some cards and bask in the sun.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Maybe I need to spell this out. Um, lean in a little, Flins.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Oh my, this doesn't bode well...

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Word is that you were caught up in a real horror show recently. People were amazed that you returned safe and sound... They've been debating whether you're even human.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I've returned safe and sound from plenty of crises. When you say "people," do you mean other people, or do you just mean you?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: ...Fine. I'll be frank. You're not human, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hahaha... Heavens, now that's a horrifying thought.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: ...You know what? Forget it! We'll revisit this once it's all over.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: A sound plan — albeit a little ominous-sounding.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: ...Just promise me you'll come back in one piece, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hah. For you, Master Illuga, how could I refuse?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Also, please pass my regards onto our colleagues. Tell them, "Thank you all for your assistance. Please, put safety first as you proceed with the operation."

talks.objective: Enter the world in the mirror
Enter the world in the mirror

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Well? Do you sense anything?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, no.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: *sigh* And this place was our last chance...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Not necessarily. We've only looked in Nasha Town so far.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Miss Columbina said she would leave messages at her friends' dwellings. It's still worth checking where Miss Lauma lives, and where I live.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Mm... Let's try and make some time to look into those then.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Wait...

talks.objective: Enter the world in the mirror

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Nothing here either...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hmm? Flins?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Ah, Miss Nefer.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What are you doing here? Unless...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I just spoke with Illuga about arrangements for the search, and came for a walk nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: As for you, why would... Huh. It appears we think along similar lines. And neither of us likes to accept things at face value.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: #As well as figuring out how to gather intel on {NICKNAME}, I wanted to confirm some of my own suspicions.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: #Also, we'll need to bring a lot of force to bear against Dottore, even if we're only looking to rescue {NICKNAME}. We can't leave anything to chance.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You don't think Columbina perished either, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I'm merely considering the possibility that she survived, just as you are. How much can we really know about a deity like her, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Do you remember what she said on Moon-Prayer Night? About using moonlight to send messages to us?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Of course. I think that's why we're both here.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Where have you checked so far?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I've been focusing on the outdoors — anywhere the moonlight shines. I checked most of Nasha Town, but didn't find anything.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I checked the Curatorium of Secrets, and a few rooms where I thought I might find some leads. But no luck here either.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The only places I haven't looked yet are the rooms in The Flagship.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: But process of elimination isn't the only thing that brought me here.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Oh really? What's your other reason?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: After all that buildup, our mystery ally never showed up even once!

dialogues.speaker: Sound
dialogues.text: (A noise is coming from indoors)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...Am I imagining things?

dialogues.speaker: Sound
dialogues.text: (A noise is coming from indoors)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...! Come on, let's see what's going on.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (...Oh no. I knocked over a vase as soon as I came in. It must have been caused by a kuuvahki fluctuation when I entered the space.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Although... It seems like I'm not about to be pulled away this time...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (It looks like as long as I'm careful with my actions, it doesn't count as "influencing" reality.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #(Anyway... Is this The Flagship? {NICKNAME} mentioned that's where {M#he}{F#she} was staying.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (I only went into the lobby last time, so I've never actually been here before... How does this space work?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (...If nothing else, I can now be sure that it is not simply "memory.")

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #({M#He}{F#She} mentioned where {M#his}{F#her} room was. I think it's... this one...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (The door is closed... but if this is anything like when I disappeared, then maybe...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #({M#He}{F#She} and Paimon aren't here at the moment...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #(I hope {M#he's}{F#she's} okay... I wonder what happened to {M#him}{F#her} after that battle with Dottore?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (... Best not to dwell on that for now. I need to try and leave them some clues.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #Please, {NICKNAME}... I really hope you find this...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...Huh. Just a cat.

dialogues.speaker: Cat
dialogues.text: Meow...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hmm... Nothing else here strikes me as noteworthy.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Didn't you stay here for a couple of nights once?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: #Before Rerir showed himself, yes. It's also where {NICKNAME} and I first met.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Did you notice anything unusual during your stay?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I remember thinking how much noisier The Flagship is at night compared to the graveyard. Other than that, no.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon were most congenial neighbors.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: This is where they've been staying, yes? Over here?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I wouldn't usually condone breaking and entering... But we can make it up to them later.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Focus now... I have to write a message on the wall using kuuvahki, just like I said on Moon-Prayer Night...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Simply open your windows on nights when the moon shines bright, and the moonlight will naturally flow towards the words I have written.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Here goes... I'll need to carefully control my strength...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #(Hmm? There's a noise outside the door... Is {M#he}{F#she} back?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Please, you have to see these words...)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Hmm? What's this?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Looks like it responds to my power...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Where does this lead? Could it be the exit?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Ad astra abyssosque! Welcome to the Adventurers' Guild.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: What? This doesn't look like Moon-Prayer Night...

dialogues.speaker: Alida
dialogues.text: Extra, extra! Get the latest Nasha Express here!

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: (I don't think I've ever been here... Maybe this space isn't comprised of my memories after all...)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: (There aren't any festive decorations around. Is this Nasha Town after Moon-Prayer Night ended?)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: (Did Dottore's plan not affect the town? Or is no one aware of what happened because he used the three moons' authority?)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: (Let me see if I can influence anyone else...)

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Have you ever wondered why we were born following such laws? Who stipulated that we could not fly instead of walk?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I have to keep searching for a path toward reality...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Sorry, this is the only way I can speak to you all right now. Please accept my apology...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Anyway, time is short. I'll cut to the chase.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: This is no ordinary Dodocommunication Device! It's my very own special modified version! Specifically...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Ah, sorry — I almost went off on another tangent there. Anyway, help yourselves.
